messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Runtime production alert: unusual p95 latency + kv-cache eviction spike observed in eu-west-1 cluster. Auto-paging the on-call rota. Alert: https://alerts.example/1745001234
Sam T: ack. I'm taking this. Pulling logs, traces, and recent deploy diffs.
Sam T: TL;DR: continuous-batching throughput jumped at ~05:12 UTC, eviction rate ~10x, and a few traces show re-used KV chunks returning unexpected seq_offset values (possible cross-request leakage).
Jordan L: Who's on-call for runtime infra? @Maria P @Alex G can you join?
Maria P: joining. Got the page. Will run quick reproducer against canary.
Alex G: initial hypothesis: batch pool key derivation lost tenant scoping somewhere in the fast path. If pool keys are global, chunk ids collide across tenants.
Priya K: This could cause content leakage between customers and also create perf cliffs when cache hits are incorrect. Marking as P1 for correctness + security.
Sam T: commands and logs I ran:
```
kubectl -n runtime-prod logs -l app=runtime --since=15m | rg "kv_cache" | tail -n 150
rg "cache_put|cache_reuse" /var/log/runtime/*.log | sed -n '1,120p'
```
Sam T: sample suspicious lines from node logs: 
```
kv_cache.put key=chunk_global_42 seq_offset=2048 size=4096 tenant=tenantA
kv_cache.reuse key=chunk_global_42 seq_offset=1024 returned_seq_offset=2048 tenant=tenantB
```
Sam T: seems like chunk ids were allocated without tenant prefix; tenantB got a chunk that was written by tenantA.
Jordan L: Did we recently roll any batching optimizations? I remember the release last week touched pool keys.
Alex G: yes — v2.13 changed serialization for pool keys to improve locality. We attempted to remove tenant_id from the hash for better reuse, and apparently that introduced the global key pool bug in the fast-path.
Maria P: I reproduced on a staging canary by running two simulated tenants concurrently. Repro snippet (sanitized):
```
python tools/simulate_load.py --tenant tA --model redwood-7b --seq 512 &
python tools/simulate_load.py --tenant tB --model redwood-7b --seq 512 &
python tools/kv_inspect.py --since 5m | jq '.entries[] | select(.key|contains("chunk_"))'
```
Maria P: Impact so far: 4 customer orgs observed incorrect outputs related to context bleed; overall rate low (~0.02% of requests) but severe for affected customers (potential data leakage/hallucination). Also saw p95 latency regressions ~2x for redwood-7b traffic during the spike.
Sam T: Mitigation options on the table: 
- Flag rollback: re-enable tenant-aware pool keys via control-plane flag (fast, no code deploy).
- Patch deploy: reintroduce tenant_id in pool key derivation and ship a canary release (requires code change + canary).
- Defensive check: on reuse verify seq_offset and tenant metadata match; drop and treat as miss if mismatch (safer but CPU heavier).
Lia M: From Product & Security perspective, flip the flag ASAP and notify affected customers.
Priya K: +1. Also gather the customer IDs so CS can reach out.
Sam T: flipping control-plane flag now: 
```
curl -sS -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/flags/kv_pool_tenant_aware" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"value": "on"}'
```
ops-bot: config-change: propagation job started (rcp-1745001234) targeting 8 runtime nodes.
Maria P: propagation status: 3/8 nodes updated, eviction rate trending down on those nodes.
Sam T: smoke test (pair tenant requests) after flip:
```
python tools/smoke_kv_isolation.py --tenants tA,tB --iterations 200
# expect zero cross-tenant reads
```
Sam T: smoke confirmed zero cross-reads on updated nodes. Holding rollout to remaining nodes until verified.
Alex G: also applying a temporary cap on continuous-batch size to reduce pool churn:
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/flags/continuous_batch_max" -d '{"value": 8}'
```
Jordan L: note: do NOT perform runtime code roll beyond the flag change until we have canary verification.
Sam T: customer impact tracking: support ticket surge from 3 accounts. Flagged cust-482, cust-901, cust-317, cust-773 as potentially affected.
Maria P: after full rollout of flag to all nodes, eviction metrics returned to baseline within ~90s, latency normalized within ~3 minutes on most hosts. No further cross-read events observed in live traces.
Priya K: what's our plan for a permanent fix?
Alex G: PR in progress to add tenant_id back to pool key, plus unit and integration tests that assert: 
- pool key includes tenant id for multi-tenant configs
- reuse only occurs when seq_offset and tenant match expected invariants
- fuzz tests to simulate concurrent pool allocations
Sam T: action items: 
- Alex G: finish PR + CI and get canary out today (target before 1745005400).
- Maria P & Jordan L: run daily kv-isolation smoke tests until release and monitor for regressions.
- Priya K & Lia M: prepare customer comms for the 4 affected accounts, include timeline and remediation.
- Ops: document rollback steps for the control-plane flag.
Sam T: handing pager to Maria for overnight. Maria, please ack and continue monitoring.
Maria P: ack. I'm on overnight. I'll leave logs + smoke outputs in the incident ticket. :thumbsup: 
ops-bot: rcp-1745001234 flagged as complete: rollout to 8/8 nodes at 05:22 UTC.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Hotfix applied (tenant-aware pooling). Status: mitigated; follow-up: permanent code change + postmortem required. Ticket: INT-1745001234
Priya K: starting postmortem draft with timeline, root cause (removed tenant_id from pool key), impact scope, and remediation plan. Meeting scheduled to review postmortem tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
Sam T: attaching canary traces and smoke logs to INT-1745001234 before I sign off.
Maria P: last cross-read observed at 05:12:48 UTC, none after 05:23:00 UTC. Marking mitigated from my side.
Lia M: notifying Sales & CS teams. Please add affected customer IDs to the ticket and notify account leads.
Jordan L: added cust-482 and cust-901 to the incident ticket.
Priya K: assigning owners for postmortem action items.
Sam T: thanks all. I'll follow up if anything else crops up.
